Draw ordered categorical outcomes from a latent variable

Source: R/draw_categorical.R
draw_ordered.Rd

Cuts a continuous latent variable at the supplied breaks to produce ordered discrete categories. A natural companion to latent-variable specifications of survey responses.

Usage

draw_ordered(
  x = latent,
  breaks,
  labels = NULL,
  N = length(x),
  strict = FALSE,
  latent = NULL,
  link = "identity",
  break_labels = NULL
)

Arguments

x

Latent continuous variable (numeric vector).

breaks

Numeric vector of cut-points in ascending order. The vector should span the range of x; values outside the range are placed in the outermost categories unless strict = TRUE. An infinite endpoint bounds the scale rather than cutting it, so c(-Inf, 0, Inf) gives the same two categories as 0.

labels

Optional character vector of category labels, one per category. That is length(breaks) + 1 for interior cut-points, one fewer for each infinite endpoint, and length(breaks) - 1 when strict = TRUE. When supplied, returns an ordered factor.

N

Must equal length(x) if it is given at all, and is an error otherwise. It cannot change how many values come back, which is always length(x): unlike draw_binary() and the rest of the family, draw_ordered() has never recycled to N, in either version. 1.x checks N against a recycling rule it does not apply.

strict

If TRUE, observations outside breaks are coded NA instead of being placed in the outermost category.

latent

Alias for x (kept for compatibility).

link

Must be "identity", the only link this function has: breaks cut the latent variable on the scale it arrives. Anything else is an error, as it is in fabricatr 1.x.

break_labels

fabricatr 1.x's name for labels. Accepted with a warning.

Value

An integer vector of category indices, one per element of x, or an ordered factor with those labels when they are supplied. With strict = TRUE, values outside breaks are NA.

Examples

fabricate(N = 200, x = rnorm(N),
          resp = draw_ordered(x, breaks = c(-1, 0, 1),
                              labels = c("disagree", "neutral",
                                         "agree", "strongly agree")))
#> # A tibble: 200 × 3
#>    ID         x resp          
#>    <chr>  <dbl> <ord>         
#>  1 001   -0.819 neutral       
#>  2 002    2.11  strongly agree
#>  3 003    1.93  strongly agree
#>  4 004    0.246 agree         
#>  5 005   -0.555 neutral       
#>  6 006    0.548 agree         
#>  7 007    1.62  strongly agree
#>  8 008    0.142 agree         
#>  9 009    0.189 agree         
#> 10 010    1.05  strongly agree
#> # ℹ 190 more rows
